detailed_summary: The paper investigates how competing quantum contacts can generate a boundary that was not present in the original specification of a subsystem. The authors construct approximately isolated bodies from the bare field vacuum using zero-centred contact packets. They show that a binding contribution with vanishing mean energy density can still alter a bounded formation signal by order one at the same clock time. On the formed material spins and their original memories, coarse collective records are shown to precede an all-outcome Bell violation. The field evolves dynamically, retaining the finite bath, residual boundary interaction, failed records, and preparation costs. The work connects dynamical subsystem formation, classical collective records, and microscopic nonlocality, with polynomial resources in the stated preparation and measurement class.
